summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style article on the Blitz, the German bombing offensive against Britain in 1940 and 1941 during the Second World War. It covers pre-war British estimates of bombing casualties, the strategic theories of air power that shaped both sides, specific raids such as those on London, Swansea and Portsmouth, German planning and navigation systems like X-Gerät, and British preparations including evacuation and blackout. It also describes Hitler's September 1940 threats and the RAF's later analysis of the campaign's effects.
one_line: Overview of the 1940-1941 German bombing offensive against Britain, covering pre-war casualty estimates, air power theory, raids, and British responses.
key_facts: After World War I the British government estimated 50 casualties, with about one third killed, would result for every tonne of bombs dropped on London.
The estimate of tonnes of bombs an enemy could drop per day grew from 75 in 1922 to 150 in 1934 and 644 in 1937.
In 1937 the Committee on Imperial Defence estimated a 60-day attack would result in 600,000 dead and 1,200,000 wounded.
On 14 October 1940, 380 German bombers from Luftflotte 3 hit London, killing around 200 people and injuring another 2,000.
British anti-aircraft defences under General Frederick Alfred Pile fired 8,326 rounds on 14 October 1940 and shot down only two bombers.
The government planned to voluntarily evacuate four million people, including 1.4 million from London, expecting about 90% to stay in private homes.
A trial blackout was held on 10 August 1939, and a blackout began at sunset when Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939.
On 4 September 1940 Hitler declared at the Sportspalast that the Luftwaffe would drop 'one million kilograms in a single night' on Britain if the RAF attacked German cities.
Giulio Douhet and Billy Mitchell espoused the idea that air forces could win wars by themselves, without land and sea fighting.
Arthur Harris, AOC Bomber Command, declared in late 1943 that Bomber Command could achieve 'a state of devastation in which surrender is inevitable.'
The X-Gerät system worked on a higher frequency (66–77 MHz) than Knickebein's 30–33 MHz and was used by specially trained pathfinder crews.
Fliegerkorps X (10th Air Corps) concentrated on mining operations against shipping and had dropped 3,984 mines by 19/20 April 1941.
Swansea was bombed four times in January 1941, and on 17 January around 100 bombers dropped some 32,000 incendiaries on it.
The term Blitz was first used by the British press as an abbreviation of Blitzkrieg (lightning war).
From 7 September 1940, London was systematically bombed by the Luftwaffe for 56 out of the following 57 days and nights.

entities.name: The Blitz
entities.role: German bombing offensive against Britain in 1940 and 1941 during the Second World War

entities.name: Luftwaffe
entities.role: German air force that conducted the bombing attacks on Britain

entities.name: Royal Air Force
entities.role: British air force whose Fighter Command defended British airspace against the Luftwaffe

entities.name: Adolf Hitler
entities.role: German leader who ordered the new bombing policy on 6 September 1940 and frustrated by the slow progress of air superiority

entities.name: Hermann Göring
entities.role: Reichsmarschall and commander-in-chief of the Luftwaffe who ordered the new policy with Hitler

entities.name: Hugh Dowding
entities.role: Air Officer Commanding Fighter Command credited with the defence of British air space

entities.name: Arthur Harris
entities.role: AOC Bomber Command who saw German morale and economy as objectives

entities.name: Frederick Alfred Pile
entities.role: General commanding British anti-aircraft defences during the 14 October 1940 raid

entities.name: Kesselring
entities.role: commander of Luftflotte 2 ordered to send 50 sorties per night against London

entities.name: Sperrle
entities.role: commander of Luftflotte 3 ordered to dispatch 250 sorties per night including 100 against the West Midlands

entities.name: Basil Liddell-Hart
entities.role: military theorist who predicted 250,000 deaths and injuries in Britain in the first week of war

entities.name: Giulio Douhet
entities.role: air power theorist who argued air forces could win wars alone

entities.name: Billy Mitchell
entities.role: air power theorist who argued air forces could win wars alone

entities.name: Ralph Ingersoll
entities.role: American publisher who visited Britain and wrote soon after the Blitz eased on 15 September

entities.name: Committee on Imperial Defence
entities.role: body that estimated 600,000 dead and 1,200,000 wounded from a 60-day attack in 1937

entities.name: Fliegerkorps X
entities.role: 10th Air Corps that concentrated on mining operations against shipping

entities.name: Bomber Command
entities.role: RAF bomber force whose policy sought victory through destruction of civilian will, communications and industry

entities.name: United States Army Air Corps
entities.role: American air force that shared the air power thinking of the RAF between the world wars

entities.name: Luftflotte 3
entities.role: German air fleet that sent 380 bombers to hit London on 14 October 1940

entities.name: London
entities.role: main target of systematic Luftwaffe bombing from 7 September 1940

entities.name: Swansea
entities.role: port city bombed four times in January, very heavily

entities.name: Portsmouth
entities.role: port city where waves of 150 bombers destroyed vast swaths of the city with 40,000 incendiaries

entities.name: West Midlands
entities.role: industrial region targeted to interfere with arms factory production

entities.name: Barcelona
entities.role: city bombed during the Spanish Civil War, supporting the 50-casualties-per-tonne estimate

entities.name: X-Gerät
entities.role: German radio navigation and bombing system used by specially trained pathfinder crews

entities.name: Knickebein
entities.role: German radio beam navigation system used en masse by German crews

entities.name: Battle of Britain
entities.role: 1940 battle for daylight air superiority between the Luftwaffe and the RAF over the UK in which the Blitz began

entities.name: Sportspalast
entities.role: venue where Hitler gave a long address on 4 September 1940
